analysis: The PR modifies only docs/architecture/inference.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date, and the patch excerpt shows prose changes in the GLM5Next video section: variable-frame-rate video is now indexed by nominalFrameRate instead of refused with a 400. The patch excerpt is truncated; additional head ranges at 876-895 and 1732-1751 are not visible in the supplied text. No code, configuration, or enforcement changes are included, so no security control regressions can be shown from this evidence. The supplied units (base lines 2366-2597, head lines 1-415) are mostly unchanged surrounding text, covering Flint, Bonsai and Nemotron Super documentation, with no changed security semantics visible. Documented behavior, including prefix-cache scoping, memory admission and bounded media decode, is consistent with the T-041 mitigations (cache scope authored by the coordinator, no cross-scope reuse for media). One residual question for integration: the GLM VFR change presumably has a code counterpart (GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset) that is not in this batch. The doc says media-decode limits remain bounded by maximumDecodedBytes (512 MiB) and the sampled-frame cap, so accepting VFR video should not widen the memory-bounded surface. If the matching code is part of this PR, a reviewer should confirm that frame-count and decoded-byte bounds are still enforced when timing is derived from nominalFrameRate (for example, a hostile track with a misleading frame rate or an enormous sample count). That code is not in the supplied evidence, so I record it as an unverified contract rather than a finding.
